transcript.text: my samsung washer dryer is making evrything smell damp/musty even after its washed, its gross. wot do i do

Musty-smelling laundry is really common with front-loaders and washer dryers, and it's usually fixable in an afternoon. The smell comes from mould, bacteria and gunk building up in hidden spots. Work through these in order:

## 1. Clean the door seal (most common culprit)
• Pull back the rubber gasket around the door and look inside the folds. You'll probably find grey/black slime, hair, fluff or even coins.
• Wipe it out with a cloth and warm water mixed with a bit of washing-up liquid, or a diluted bleach solution (about 1 part bleach to 10 parts water). Wear gloves.
• Dry it thoroughly afterwards.

## 2. Clean the drain/debris filter
• On most Samsung models it's behind a small flap at the bottom front corner.
• Put towels and a shallow tray down first. There'll be a small drain hose to let water out, then unscrew the filter.
• It's often full of smelly sludge, fluff and bits. Rinse it, wipe the housing, and screw it back in tightly.

## 3. Clean the detergent drawer
• Pull it right out (there's usually a release tab in the softener section).
• Scrub off the mouldy residue with an old toothbrush and hot water.
• Shine a torch into the drawer cavity too. The roof of it often gets mouldy, so give that a scrub.

## 4. Run a drum clean
• Use the Drum Clean / Self Clean cycle with the drum empty.
• Add a washing machine cleaner (e.g. Dr. Beckmann Service-It) or about 1 cup of soda crystals or white vinegar in the drum. Don't mix vinegar and bleach.
• If the smell's bad, run it twice.

## 5. Change your habits so it doesn't come back
• Leave the door and drawer ajar between washes so it dries out. This is the big one.
• Take laundry out promptly. Wet clothes left sitting will go musty fast.
• Use less detergent than you think. Excess builds up into gunk. Same goes for fabric softener, which is a major cause of buildup.
• Do a hot wash (60°C) at least once a week, e.g. towels or bedding. Constant 30°C washes let bacteria thrive.
• Run the drum clean monthly. Samsung machines often show a reminder.
• Don't overload, especially when using the drying function.

## If it still smells after all that
• Check the drain hose isn't kinked or pushed too far down the waste pipe, as that can let dirty water siphon back.
• Clothes that already smell might need a rewash with a laundry sanitiser or a scoop of oxygen bleach (e.g. Vanish) on a hot wash, because the smell can cling to fabric.
• If it persists, it could be a drainage fault, and Samsung support or a repair engineer is worth calling.

Nine times out of ten, the door seal plus the debris filter plus a drum clean sorts it. Good luck! 🧺

ok thanks, thats a lot lol. ive had a look at the door seal and theres black spots and grey sludge in the bottom fold. drawer is rank too, slimy black stuff in the softener bit. will try cleaning those and the filter, anything else i should know?

Sounds like you've found the culprits. A few extra tips:

Door seal
• The grey sludge should wipe out easily, but black spots are mould that's grown into the rubber, so they often won't fully scrub off. A diluted bleach solution left on for 10–15 minutes before wiping can lighten them. Some people soak kitchen roll in it and tuck it into the fold.
• If it's still stained but no longer smells, that's fine. If it's cracked, torn or still smells after cleaning, a replacement seal is fairly cheap (find the model number on the sticker inside the door).

Drawer
• That slime in the softener bit is classic softener buildup. Consider using less softener or ditching it. Towels in particular dry fluffier and more absorbent without it.
• Check the cavity the drawer slides into, especially the roof. It's usually just as bad up there.

Filter
• More water comes out than you'd expect, so have a few towels and a baking tray ready. Make sure it's screwed back in firmly or it'll leak.

Then finish off
• Once those are clean, run the Drum Clean cycle empty (with a machine cleaner or soda crystals) to flush out the rest of the gunk.
• Re-wash anything that smells musty on a hot wash afterwards.

Going forward, the two big ones are: leave the door and drawer open between washes, and get clothes out as soon as the cycle finishes. That alone stops most of this from coming back.
